messages:
maria: Quick follow-up from yesterday's RFC — I prototyped a way to decompose tenant fairness into two orthogonal controls: a static weight (long window) and a dynamic penalty (short window). Wanted to share results and solicit tuning ideas before we land the refactor.

chen: ooh nice, can you drop the perf numbers?

maria: 10k qps synthetic mix: tail latency improved ~8% at p99 for noisy tenants, overall throughput same. penalty reduced wasted capacity in bursty tenants.

david: sounds promising. any oscillation / thrashing? last time we added a dynamic term it bounced under mixed load.

maria: good call — saw mild oscillation at the 30s scale when penalty learning rate was high. I added dampening + min-duration thresholds and that stabilized.

ryan: curious about metrics we used for the penalty signal. is it queue depth? token-per-request?

maria: primary signal = moving-window excess-requests ratio (requests over fair-share) + KV-cache-miss rate as a modifier. formula in the snippet below.

maria: ```
penalty_t = clamp(base_penalty + alpha * excess_ratio - beta * cache_hit_modifier, 0, max_penalty)
apply_penalty(tenant) {
  admission_prob = sigmoid(log_budget - penalty_t)
  // probabilistic admission to avoid hard evictions
}
```

alex: neat. How do we pick alpha/beta? manual or auto?

maria: initially manual but we ran a small grid and then a hill-climb online tuning with safety bounds. We keep a monotonicity invariant so increasing excess can't lower penalty.

chen: can we make the penalty signal composable with existing quota tokens? e.g., penalty reduces token drain rate instead of admission prob. That might be less surprising for other systems.

maria: yes, we experimented with both: modifying token drain (smooth) vs admission prob (spikier). Drain-rate approach produced steadier latency but slightly higher cost.

ryan: telemetry ask — add these traces: tenant, excess_ratio, penalty_t, admission_prob, token_drain_rate. Also flag when we hit min-duration dampening so we can see oscillation sources.

maria: will add. plan: run canary on 10 tenants for 48h, then widen. looking for reviewers on the rollout gating policy and safety thresholds.

david: +1 on canary. two asks: (1) add a kill-switch that sets penalty=0 for a tenant and routes to fallback model; (2) hard limit on cumulative rejections per tenant per hour so we don't regress UX silently.

maria: both reasonable. I'll add a tenant-level override in the control plane and an alert if rejection-rate > threshold.

chen: one more — consider a "stability gradient" config for each env (prod vs staging) so alpha is lower in prod by default. Less tuning risk.

maria: agreed. that'll be a per-deployment parameter. Also thinking of an automated policy to lower alpha during large infra events (region flaps).

infra-bot: deploybot: canary rollout scheduled for "fairpenalty-v1" to infra-canary cluster at 2024-11-02T09:30:00Z by maria.

alex: can we pair a small chaos test (latency spike + cache flush) to validate stability?

maria: yes, adding a chaos scenario to the canary runbook: spike RPS + 60s cache invalidation pattern.

ryan: I'll prepare the dashboards and a short eval script to compute regret vs baseline.

maria: thanks all. I'll post the canary playbook link here when ready. please ping if you want to be on-call for the first window. :rocket:
